text: AD 64. Rome burns. Nero plays the fiddle.
Nope. Wrong instrument. Wrong place.
Nero: the fiddling myth.
First: fiddles didn't exist yet.
The violin came along 1,500 years later.
Romans had the lyre.
Second: Nero wasn't even in Rome.
He was at his villa in Antium, miles away.
When he heard, he rushed back.
He opened his gardens to the homeless.
And brought in food from nearby towns.
So where did the music come from?
It was a rumour.
People said he sang about the fall of Troy.
Even the historian Tacitus called it a rumour.
But Nero was unpopular. So it stuck.
Was Nero a good emperor? Not really.
But he didn't fiddle.
Fiddles in ancient Rome: zero.
Anyway, here's Nero fiddling.
